specification.problem: Characterize which two-outcome generalized measurements (Kraus operators with given singular values) can be decomposed into a sequence of weak measurements, each from a system-qubit probe interaction with constant Hamiltonian, interleaved with arbitrary unitary pulses and feedback.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One iteration of a weak measurement with a qubit probe, a tiny qubit-system instance, and the composition of iterations into a two-outcome Kraus operator with two distinct singular values. Excluded: the paper's characterization proof, the explicit Hamiltonian and pulse schedule, the continuous-time limit, and the feedback control rule.

equations.label: Two-outcome completeness
equations.description: Completeness relation for a two-outcome generalized measurement.
equations.justification: Standard definition of a two-outcome generalized measurement; the abstract only names such measurements.

equations.label: Weak measurement via probe
equations.description: Kraus operators on the system from a probe interaction followed by a probe measurement in a computational basis.
equations.justification: The abstract describes a qubit probe with constant interaction Hamiltonian but gives no form. This is the standard construction, with an assumed probe readout basis and initial probe state.
assumptions: Probe is read out in the computational basis

equations.label: Iterated feedback composition
equations.description: Product of weak-measurement Kraus operators interleaved with unitary pulses; a trajectory outcome record j is later coarse-grained into the two outcomes of the target measurement.
equations.abstract_quote: even given the ability to perform arbitrary unitary pulses throughout the continuous decomposition
equations.justification: Inferred from the stated iterated weak measurements with unitary pulses; the coarse-graining rule is not given.
assumptions: Stopping rule and outcome coarse-graining are unspecified

equations.label: Singular-value constraint on achievable measurements
equations.description: Singular value decomposition of an achievable Kraus operator; the abstract states that only measurements with two distinct singular values are achievable, which is the generic qubit case.
equations.abstract_quote: only generalized measurements with two distinct singular values are achievable
equations.justification: Direct reading of the abstract claim stated as an SVD, which is a standard background tool; the exact condition is paraphrased.
assumptions: Applies to qubit system, per Kraus operator

registers.name: P
registers.role: probe for each weak measurement iteration, fresh per iteration (assumed)

specification.initial_state: System in an arbitrary state |psi>; a fresh probe in |0> for each iteration (assumed).

steps.description: Prepare a fresh probe qubit in |0>.
Apply a system unitary pulse U_k, then evolve under the constant H_SP for a short time.
Measure the probe to obtain outcome j_k and update the system with K_{j_k}.
Repeat with feedback-chosen pulses until a stopping condition, then compare the accumulated operator to the target M_a.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the probe after each interaction (assumed).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Feedback rule choosing the next pulse and the final assignment of the outcome record to M_0 or M_1; neither is specified in the abstract.
assumptions: Probe readout basis, probe initial state, and the form of H_SP are assumed
Instance is a single system qubit
missing_information: Stopping criterion and coarse-graining of outcomes
Precise characterization theorem and continuous-time limit
